hero.headline: Your data has a home now.
hero.sub: One lakehouse with dashboards built in. Bring every source in, keep it in open tables, and ask for answers in plain language.

sources.headline: Everything flows in.
sources.sub: Databases, files, streams, APIs and business apps land in one place, on a schedule or as they change.
sources.caption: Live change capture for PostgreSQL. Dedupe or keep history on load, discover tables in any source, and upload 10 files at once, in folders.

bronze.title: As it came.
bronze.body: Every source lands untouched in open Apache Iceberg tables. Nothing is changed, nothing is lost.

silver.title: Cleaned and checked.
silver.body: Pipelines drop duplicates, fix spellings and join the sources. Quality checks flag what is still wrong.

gold.title: Ready for answers.
gold.body: Tables built for your questions, refreshed within the lag you set. Dashboards and the assistant read from here.

card.bronzeNote: Stored as sent, every row kept

sr.bronze: Illustration: five order rows from an orders file and a CRM export, stored as they came. One order arrives twice, Jakarta is spelt three ways, the dates use three formats and one amount is missing.
sr.silver: Illustration: the same rows in one Silver table. The duplicate is gone, every city reads Jakarta or Bandung, every date has one format, and a quality check flags the one empty amount.
sr.gold: Illustration: a Gold table of revenue by city built from those rows, Jakarta first, then Bandung, within its target lag, ready for dashboards and the assistant.

assistant.headline: Ask, don't dig.
assistant.sub: The assistant works with the same tools as the console. It answers questions, builds charts and dashboards, and runs pipelines. Anything risky waits for a person to approve it. Prefer SQL? Query Studio has autocomplete, tabs and a query history.
assistant.caption: Illustration
assistant.userOne: Which region had the most visitors last quarter?
assistant.answerOne: Region North had the most visitors last quarter.
assistant.srDescription: An illustration of the assistant. A person asks which region had the most visitors last quarter and the assistant answers with a small bar chart. The person then asks to pause the nightly sales pipeline, and the assistant shows a card that waits for a person to approve or decline the change. The region names and numbers are illustrative.

dashboards.headline: Answers come back up as dashboards.
dashboards.sub: About two dozen chart types, maps on your own boundaries included.
features: Public links with expiry and password
dashboards.caption: Illustrations, not customer data.

governance.headline: Guarded by default.
governance.sub: Roles decide who sees what, down to the column.
governance.tableCaption: Five fictional customers. As an analyst the name and email columns are masked; as an admin they are shown in full.

status.analyst: Showing as Analyst: names and emails masked
status.admin: Showing as Admin: every column in full

governance.piiTip: Personal data, masked for roles without access

lineage.title: Column-level lineage
lineage.line: See where every column comes from, raw to curated.

proof.title: Masking, tested
proof.line: An automated acceptance test checks it end to end.

audit.title: Every action, logged
audit.line: Risky assistant actions wait for a person.

catalog.title: A catalog you can trust
catalog.line: Search, then see what is certified or deprecated.

access.title: Access per folder
access.line: Permissions per dashboard and per folder.

cards.title: Open source.
cards.body: AGPL-3.0. Read every line, run it yourself.

cards.title: Open tables.
cards.body: Raw data in Apache Iceberg. Any engine that reads Iceberg can read it.

cards.title: Your servers or ours.
cards.body: Install it on your own infrastructure, or talk to us about running it for you.

console.label: The console, as you will run it
console.caption: Its home: ask a question in plain words, or start from a shortcut to connect a source, create a pipeline or build a dashboard.
console.alt: The RantAI Lakehouse console's home: a box to ask the assistant, with Ask, Build and Tools, and three shortcuts: Connect a source, Create a pipeline and Build a dashboard.

getStarted.headline: Up and running in three steps.

steps.title: Clone it
steps.note: The public repository, with everything the stack needs.

steps.title: Configure it
steps.note: This writes `.env` with generated secrets. Then set `AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL` and `AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD` in it: that is your first account.

steps.title: Start it
steps.note: Then open `http://localhost:3000` and sign in with that account.

final.headline: Come on in. The data's fine.
